decision: Can one runtime flag preserve the qualified DP lattice precision on both the standard motion environment and Thor without platform-specific planner code?
invariants: the same planner source runs on x86 and Thor
the qualified default disables TF32 before torch initializes cuBLAS
malformed values fail before the planner starts
objectives, tolerances, search budgets, and planner outputs are unchanged
judges: torch reports allow_tf32 false and highest float32 matmul precision
float32 and float64 lattice screens agree above the committed threshold
candidate failed-test set introduces no failures relative to the same-runtime baseline
free-space failures are compared against untouched olp-export under the same runtime rather than required to be absolutely green
contract_correction: Evidence forced the free-space judge from absolute-green to differential: the strict runtime exposes two identical failures on untouched olp-export and the candidate. This follows the pre-registered differential promotion rule and does not waive a candidate regression.
